newsitem.title: UK: ICI sees rebound in 1997, may float Tioxide.
newsitem.headline: ICI sees rebound in 1997, may float Tioxide.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc reported a slip in 1996 results on Thursday, as it had predicted, but said it looked forward to better results in 1997 and was considering separating out its Tioxide operatons, "with a view to flotation."

ICI said its pretax profits before exceptional charges fell in 1996 to 603 million pounds ($967 million) from 951 million in 1995, and the result was near the lower end of analysts expectations which had ranged from 575 to 650 million pounds.
In the fourth quarter, when pretax profit fell to 105 million pounds from 193 million, earnings per share before exceptional items halved to 7.5 pence from 15 pence.

In his comments, company chairman Sir Ronald Hampel said the results again reflected the dominance of the cyclical industrial chemicals market, and he explained the Tioxide plan was part of an aim to shift its portfolio towards less cyclical businesses.
"1996 was a difficult year for the global chemical industry, with significant downward pressure on prices and margins.

"The hard won progress in delivering the value gap and in reshaping the business portfolio, together with an outstanding performance in ICI's growing paint's business, were offset by the large cyclical price movements in industrial chemicals," he added.

Looking to the outlook for the industrial chemicals market, the company said it saw "indications that the substantial price erosion which took place through the year may have bottomed in the fourth quarter in some sectors, notably chlorine, PTA (purified terephthalic acid) and titanium.
